Main.sentence: Steeler Nation is an official name for the ___E:fan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_(person))___ base of the ___E:National Football League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League)___ 's ___E:Pittsburgh Steelers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers)___ .

The term was coined by ___E:NFL Films U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Films)___ narrator ___E:John Facenda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Facenda)___ in the team's 1978 highlights film. Steelers Country is often used for the ___E:Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh)___ , area where the fan base originates or for areas with a large Steelers fan base.

The Steelers have had a following in ___E:Western Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Pennsylvania)___ since 1933. That year, ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania)___ relaxed its ___E:blue laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_law)___ allowing sporting events in the commonwealth on Sundays, paving the way for the Steelers and the ___E:Philadelphia Eagles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles)___ to begin play for the ___E:1933 NFL season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_NFL_season)___ .

Previously, the state had teams in ___E:Pottsville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottsville,_Pennsylvania)___ and ___E:Frankford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankford,_Philadelphia,_Pennsylvania)___ , but both had already folded, due to both the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ and their inability to play on Sunday, when most NFL games took place.

Much like the league itself in the early years, the Steelers had to compete with baseball and ___E:college football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football)___ teams in the city, making the team third in the hierarchy to the ___E:Pittsburgh Pirates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates)___ and the ___E:Pitt Panthers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers_football)___ .

Despite the team's early struggles, it had a small but loyal fan base in the city due to the popularity of ___E:American football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ at all levels, dating back to the 1800s, when Pittsburgh hosted the first wholly professional football game in 1895.
By the 1950s, the Steelers had gained some popularity in the city and were on par with Pitt, but they were still a distant second behind the Pirates in the city.
In the early 1970s, the Steelers began to rise in popularity.

In 1969, there was the hiring of head coach ___E:Chuck Noll U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Noll)___ and the drafting of future ___E:Hall of Fame U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Football_Hall_of_Fame)___ ___E:defensive tackle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_tackle)___ ___E:"Mean Joe" Greene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Greene)___ . ___E:By 1972 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season)___ , the Steelers were a playoff contender and began a sellout streak in ___E:Three Rivers Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Rivers_Stadium)___ that carried over to ___E:Heinz Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz_Field)___ and still stands to this day. The team is second to the ___E:Washington Commanders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders)___ for the longest active consecutive sellout streak in league history.

The team's four Super Bowl victories in the 1970s coincided with a ___E:recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recession)___ that struck the United States, and the city in particular, that would lead to the closure of several steel mills in the early 1980s.

The team's success was credited with giving people in the city hope and leading to the increased fan base. Due to economic uncertainty in the area, many Steelers fans relocated to other areas but retained their identification with the Steelers as a reflection of their former hometown's steel industrial base.

During the lead up to ___E:Super Bowl XIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XIII)___ between the Steelers and the ___E:Dallas Cowboys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys)___ , Phil Musick contrasted the Dallas and Pittsburgh fans by saying that "Dallas is superfan ___E:Whistling Ray U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_Ray)___ and a hat that sprays the unsuspecting with water; Pittsburgh is a guy in a ___E:gorilla suit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorilla_suit)___ who'll stove five of your ribs if you laugh at him."

___E:Jack Lambert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Lambert_(American_football))___ said of Steeler Nation during his Hall of Fame induction speech: "How lucky I was to have played for the Pittsburgh Steelers fans. A proud, hard-working people, who loves their football, and their players."
In the 1970s many fans organized fan clubs for their favorite players.

Some of these fan clubs included ___E:Franco's Italian Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Harris)___ ,  ___E:Frenchy's Foreign Legion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fuqua)___ ,   ___E:Gerela's Gorillas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Gerela)___ ,    ___E:Bradshaw's Brigade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Bradshaw)___ ,  ___E:Lambert's Lunatics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Lambert_(American_football))___ ,   Dobre Shunka (Good Ham, for ___E:Jack Ham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ham)___ ),  ___E:Rocky and the Flying Squirrels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Bleier)___ ,  ___E:Shell's Bombers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donnie_Shell)___ , and ___E:Russell's Raiders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Russell_(American_football))___ .

Since the 1970s, the Steelers have enjoyed a large fan base and have eclipsed the ___E:Pittsburgh Pirates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Pirates)___ as the most popular sports team in Pittsburgh.

While the team's success gained it a large fan base nationally, many consider the collapse of the city's steel industry to have been a cause for the strong fan base in other cities, demonstrated when teams whose home turnout would otherwise require a local ___E:blackout U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_blackout)___ on television end up selling out when hosting the Steelers.

An instance of the team's large fan base was at ___E:Super Bowl XL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL)___ , where an ESPN.com columnist suggested that Steelers fans outnumbered ___E:Seattle Seahawks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Seahawks)___ fans more than 25–1  though that may have to do with the geographical closeness of ___E:Ford Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Field)___ to Pittsburgh.

In November 2007, a study by Turnkey Sports found that the Steelers brand was the strongest in its local market of any team in the ___E:NHL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL)___ , ___E:NBA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA)___ , ___E:MLB U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB)___ or ___E:NFL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL)___ .

Many regional communities not officially associated with the "Pittsburgh" market have overwhelming numbers of Steeler fans who regularly flood local stations in both ___E:Harrisburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrisburg,_Pennsylvania)___     and ___E:Erie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erie,_Pennsylvania)___ with requests to show the technically "out of market" Steeler games.
___E:Hines Ward U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hines_Ward)___ 's victory on Dancing With The Stars could also be seen as a sign of the national reach of the Steelers' fan base.

In November 2007, ___E:NFL Films U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Films)___ president and co-founder ___E:Steve Sabol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Sabol)___ speaking at the team's 75th anniversary gala at the ___E:David L. Lawrence Convention Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_L._Lawrence_Convention_Center)___ stated: "The Steelers don't need a mascot.

Their fans are their mascot...There were Gerela's Gorillas, Franco's Italian Army, Lambert's Lunatics, people dressed up like a bumble bee. You don't need a mascot when you have fans like that. When we'd go to Pittsburgh to do the game for NFL Films we never brought enough cameras."

Human resources recruiters from the ___E:natural gas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas)___ industry, particularly those in the ___E:Marcellus Shale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcellus_Formation)___ where Pittsburgh is located, began targeting Steeler bars nationwide for possible employees.
Attempts at quantifying the loyalty of Steeler Nation relative to other NFL fan bases have shown mixed results.

A 2006 study by the ___E:American City Business Journals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_City_Business_Journals)___ placed the team's fans 21st out of 32 teams in the league,  behind all three of its division rivals in the ___E:AFC North U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_North)___ .

The study found that although the team had been selling out games for years, some fans were not actually attending the games, and Pittsburgh's weekly turnout percentage for home games was 16th in the league.

That ranking was down seven slots from the publication's survey conducted in 1997, which ranked Steelers Nation 14th out of 30 teams, partly due to fans leaving nearly 10% of the seats in the stadium empty.

On the other hand, a 2008 study from ___E:Forbes.com U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes.com)___ ranked Steelers fans 8th overall, citing among other things a long season-ticket waiting list.  A 2008 article for ESPN.com ranked Steelers fans as the best in the NFL, citing their "unbelievable" sellout streak of 299 consecutive games.

Anti–Steeler Nation sentiment has grown strong enough that in some cases, ___E:front offices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_office_(sports))___ for other teams have taken steps to keep Pittsburgh fans out of games in their cities.

Instead of being permitted to buy tickets to a ___E:Chargers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers)___ –Steelers game in San Diego, for instance, they were required to pay for tickets to two other games, as well.  In other cases, teams refused to sell tickets to fans calling from Pittsburgh's 412 ___E:area code U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_code)___ , and they encouraged fans who were selling their own tickets to do the same.  Steelers President ___E:Art Rooney II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Rooney_II)___ complained to the NFL about the situation, but his grievance was not acted upon.
